newsitem.title: USA: Firm recalls 63,000 seat rings on Entertainers.
newsitem.headline: Firm recalls 63,000 seat rings on Entertainers.

text.p: Graco Children's Products Inc said Monday it was recalling and providing a free replacement for the white plastic seat rings in some 63,000 of its stationary Entertainers made before March 1996.

The Elverson, Pa.,-based maker of children's strollers, swings, high chairs and related products, acknowledged in a statement that the seat rings have sharp edges that can cut, scratch or scrape a child's legs.
The product was sold nationwide in juvenile products and discount stores beginning in November 1995 for $59 to $69 it said.

The company described the product as having a plastic tray measuring 27 inches across that is supported by three adjustable legs. A chair sits in the center of the unit and can be swivelled so the child can play with toys attached to the tray. The white plastic seat ring is located under the padded seat cover.
It said it has received more than 400 complaints of injuries to children, usually as they were lifted from the seat, it said.
Barbara Riggins, a spokeswoman for the company, said none of the injuries reported were serious "and required no medical attention." She said Graco's recall was voluntarily decided by the company.
The company said the replacement seat ring can be installed at home by simply snapping it into place. It said Entertainers with yellow seat rings are not involved in the recall.
It said that consumers should stop using the pre-March 1996 Entertainers immediately.
